deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW (my interpretation). The page is a numerical test of a projective-geometry relation. The setup has two lines A, B and two points a, b in one plane, and two lines A', B' and two points a', b' in a second plane (or a second copy of the plane). Following Gauss's notation, 'pL' means the value of the linear form of line L at point p. This value is proportional to the signed distance of p from L.

(1) GENERAL RELATIONS (top left). Gauss writes
  XA'·aA / (XA·a'A') = XB'·aB / (XB·a'B'),
whose cross-multiplied form is the first two lines:
  XA·aB·XB'·a'A' = XA'·a'B'·XB·aA.
Below it he notes 'X bA, b'A'': the same relation with b, b' in place of a, a'.

Read as a collineation X -> X' that sends A->A', B->B', a->a', b->b' (the X on the primed side should be the image point X'), the relation says
  [X'A'/X'B'] : [XA/XB] = [a'A'/a'B'] : [aA/aB].
This is the transport of the ratio of two linear forms, which a collineation changes only by a constant factor.

The same relation with b in place of a gives a second expression for that constant. Equating the two (my step) gives the compatibility condition
  aA·bB·a'B'·b'A' = aB·bA·a'A'·b'B'.
Equivalently, (aA·bB)/(aB·bA) is a projective invariant of two lines and two points: a cross ratio of a, b, ab∩A, ab∩B. It must agree for the two configurations.

(2) NUMERICAL DATA.
- Lines:
  A = -3x - 6y + 72,
  B = 5x - 4y + 20,
  A' = -4x - 9y + 45,
  B' = -x + y + 3 (the -x is needed; see corrections).
- Points:
  a = (3, 0),
  b = (9, 1),
  a' = (305/50, 311/50),
  b' = (25/7, 40/7).

(3) EVALUATIONS.
- Unprimed side:
  Aa = -9 + 72 = 63,
  Ab = -27 - 6 + 72 = 39,
  Ba = 15 + 20 = 35,
  Bb = 45 - 4 + 20 = 61.
- Primed side (Gauss's labels 'Aa'', 'Ab'' etc. are A'(a'), A'(b'), B'(a'), B'(b')):
  A'(a') = (-1220 - 2799 + 2250)/50 = -1769/50,
  A'(b') = (-100 - 360 + 315)/7 = -145/7,
  B'(a') = (-305 + 311 + 150)/50 = 156/50,
  B'(b') = (-25 + 40 + 21)/7 = 36/7.
- The scratch column (-100, -360, -2799 +315, +2250, and probably -1220) holds exactly these partial products.

(4) INVARIANT CHECK (bottom line). Gauss writes 63·145·156·61 over 1769·39·35·36. This is
  [Aa·Bb·B'a'·(-A'b')] versus [(-A'a')·Ab·Ba·B'b'],
with the denominators 50 and 7 cancelling and the two minus signs cancelling. Both products equal 86 928 660. So the cross-ratio invariants of the configurations (A, B, a, b) and (A', B', a', b') agree, and the relation in (1) is consistent.

(5) SIDE NOTES. The fraction (-4x - 9y + 45)/(-3x - 6y + 72) = A'/A in the middle is a side remark, presumably toward the linear-fractional form of the map. '-9 - 6x' is an unclear scratch.

The page has no connection with the elliptic-function note on the recto.
errors: No arithmetic errors: all eight evaluations and the final product equality check out.
Notational looseness: in the general relation Gauss writes XA' where (under the collineation reading) the image point X' is meant.
Gauss labels the values A'(a') etc. as 'Aa'', 'Ab'', 'Ba'', 'Bb'' without a prime on the line.

results.what: Relation transporting the ratio of two linear forms (signed distances to two lines) through a correspondence fixed by a point pair; the resulting consistency condition aA·bB·a'B'·b'A' = aB·bA·a'A'·b'B'
results.modern_name: Projective invariant (cross ratio) of a configuration of two lines and two points; compatibility condition for a planar collineation
results.usually_credited_to: Cross ratio/projective invariants: Möbius (1827), Chasles, Steiner, Plücker (1820s–1830s)

results.what: Numerical verification with explicit lines and points that the invariants agree (both products = 86928660)
results.modern_name: Numerical check of a cross-ratio equality

deep.surprise_reason: Routine projective/analytic geometry: Gauss checks a cross-ratio-type invariant on a constructed numerical example. Such invariants were standard by the 1830s–40s; the page is a computational worksheet, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: B' line: should read 'B'  -x + y + 3'; the -x is part of the formula (required for B'(a')=156/50 and B'(b')=36/7) and should not be marked deleted.
Scratch column: '-160' should be '-360' (= -9·40), and '-2299' should be '-2799' (= -9·311); '-1220' (= -4·305) appears to be present as well.
Fraction denominator: '[-+-]3x - 6y + 72' should read '-3x - 6y + 72' (the form A).
Third formula: the denominator term is probably a'A' (with prime on the line), i.e. XA'·aA/(XA·a'A') = XB'·aB/(XB·a'B').
Labels 'Aa'', 'Ab'', 'Ba'', 'Bb'' denote A'(a'), A'(b'), B'(a'), B'(b').
